The Executive Director of the Office of Rights, Compliance and Accountability (ORCA) provides strategic, university\-wide leadership to advance a safe, respectful, accessible, and welcoming learning and working environment while ensuring compliance with federal and state laws, Board of Regents Policy, and University regulations. Reporting to the Associate Vice Chancellor of Student Affairs, this position oversees the administration of ORCA, including associate directors, investigators, case managers, and professional staff, while providing executive oversight of Title IX, ADA/Section 504, Clery Act, student conduct, CARE, civil rights compliance, and related institutional compliance programs. Serving as the University's ADA/504 Coordinator and Chief Student Conduct Officer, the Executive Director helps coordinate and at times leads investigations involving discrimination, harassment, sexual misconduct, student misconduct, accessibility, and other complaints; develops and implements institutional policies, procedures, and prevention strategies; oversees the university's threat assessment and CARE teams; manages compliance reporting and case management systems; and serves as the primary resource for complex compliance matters across the institution. The Executive Director collaborates extensively with university leadership, faculty, staff, students, community partners, and external agencies to promote a culture of accountability, safety, and respect through education, training, outreach, policy development, and continuous improvement while managing departmental operations, personnel, and budget in support of the university's academic, research, and student success missions.



To thrive in this role, the successful candidate will possess a thorough knowledge of federal and state civil rights and higher education laws, as well as demonstrated experience interpreting and applying complex laws, regulations, policies, and higher education best practices. You will be an accomplished leader with experience managing professional staff, fostering collaboration, and building strong partnerships across diverse stakeholder groups. The successful candidate will demonstrate exceptional analytical, investigative, critical thinking, and problem\-solving skills, along with the ability to exercise sound judgment in sensitive and complex situations. Strong written and verbal communication skills are essential, as is the ability to effectively engage with a wide array of communities. Experience with case management databases and enterprise systems, such as Banner, is highly desirable, along with a strong understanding of trauma\-informed practices and their application in investigations, student conduct, and civil rights compliance.

The Director of Operations position is full\-time, 40 hours per week (exempt, benefits eligible). The Director of Operations reports to the Chief Operations Officer and provides leadership and operational support to Directors across all New Life Centers locations. * Provide leadership and oversight for operational departments, including Information Technology, Office Management, Transportation, Safety, Facilities, and Events.
* Establish operational priorities and lead the achievement of short\- and long\-term goals.
* Serve as a primary point of contact for operational matters, responding to urgent issues as needed.
* Travel regularly between sites to provide support, oversight, and operational leadership.

#### **Strategic Planning \& Process Improvement**

* Research, develop, and recommend process improvements, systems, and operational solutions for executive review and approval.
* Lead organization\-wide implementation and adoption of new operational processes and systems.
* Balance site\-level operational needs with broader organizational objectives when developing solutions.
* Foster collaboration across locations and departments to strengthen organizational alignment and reduce operational silos.

* Collaborate with department leaders to maintain accountability and consistency in operational practices.

* Promote and integrate safety considerations into operational planning, process development, and problem\-solving.
* Participate in organizational audits and support the implementation of corrective actions when necessary.
* Monitor operational systems and address issues through timely troubleshooting and resolution.

new_jobs.title: Manager, Office of the CEO
new_jobs.description:
**Organization Overview**


GreenLight Fund is a national nonprofit with a local focus that partners with communities to create opportunities for inclusive prosperity.  

  

We facilitate a community\-driven process that matches the local needs of individuals and families not met by existing programs, to organizations with track records of success elsewhere. Working with communities, we identify, invite in and launch proven organizations, providing collaborative support so they can quickly take root and deliver change. Everything we do is designed to remove barriers to inclusive prosperity all too often rooted in racial inequities. Our impact increases exponentially as we address one specific, community\-identified need each year, in each GreenLight site.  

  

To date, we have brought 63 evidence\-based portfolio organizations across 14 sites, invested $41M, and attracted an additional $364M from other funding sources, reaching nearly 1\.3M individuals and families this past year alone.

  

To learn more about the GreenLight Fund, please visit www.greenlightfund.org.

**Position Overview**


The Manager, Office of the CEO will help strengthen the effectiveness of GreenLight’s Office of the CEO by supporting planning, coordination, communication, and follow\-through on key organizational priorities. This role works closely with the Chief of Staff and CEO to help move important work forward across the Board of Directors, National Advisory Council, Executive Team, Leadership Team, annual planning, and cross\-functional projects.

Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory invites visionary, accomplished communications leaders to apply for the role of **Chief Communications Officer** (CCO)—a rare opportunity to shape the voice and reputation of one of the world's premier scientific research institutions. The CCO will lead Berkeley Lab's strategic communications function and help advance the Laboratory's mission of delivering science solutions to the world's greatest challenges.

  



Reporting directly to the Laboratory Director and serving as a key member of the executive leadership team, the Chief Communications Officer is a trusted strategic advisor who partners closely with senior leaders to advance Berkeley Lab's scientific, operational, fiscal, cultural, and reputational goals. Leading the 17\-person Strategic Communications Office, the CCO will develop and execute a bold, integrated communications strategy that elevates the Laboratory's global profile, strengthens engagement with the U.S. Department of Energy, the University of California, policymakers, scientific collaborators, employees, and surrounding communities, and reinforces Berkeley Lab's position as a world leader in scientific innovation.

new_jobs.title: Executive Director of Facilities
new_jobs.description:
Responsible for overseeing the operation, maintenance, and managerial oversight of multiple buildings (operational (open 24/7/365\) and residential); implementing policies, procedures, and programs that will assure well\-managed, well\-maintained buildings and equipment; leading staff in a positive service response to the concerns and needs of employees and tenants; providing assurance of safety concerns, quality programs, NYC code compliance and policy compliance, in coordination and conjunction with the company goals. This position serves as an exemplary leader and develops and maintains excellent working relationships with AMC employees/tenants, the community, and regulatory and city and state agencies. The ED assumes financial accountability, people management of direct reports, manages key performance indicators, and executes the strategic directives of AMC.


### **Key Responsibilities**


* Maintains complete responsibility and oversight of day\-to\-day operations of hospital and other facilities, ensuring that all services are effectively delivered and building needs are met including, custodial, life\-safety, housing, security, risk management, engineering, and general and preventative maintenance (including medical equipment); ensures that staff implements and provides these services in a manner consistent with the policies, goals, and objectives.
* Provides leadership in programming, budgeting, and full oversight of campus capital program instantiates annually.
* In collaboration with Finance identify campus utilities reduction opportunities and operational efficiency.
* Directly oversees campus asset NYC code compliance and regulatory compliance to NYC Local Laws.
* Provide exemplary leadership to management team including prioritization, direction, development, and assessment.
* Implementing policies, procedures and programs that will assure well\-managed, well\-maintained buildings and equipment
* Lead staff in a positive service response to the concerns and needs of employees and tenants
* Provide assurance of safety concerns, quality programs, NYC code compliance and policy compliance, in coordination and conjunction with the organization's goals.
* Lead, develop, maintain an excellent working relationships with employees, tenants, the community, and regulatory and city and state agencies.
* Assumes financial accountability, people management of direct reports, manages key performance indicators and executes the strategic directives of the organization.
* Oversee the planning and operation of facilities in emergency response situations, disaster preparedness, and emergency notification programs.
* Advises C\-Suite leadership on operational improvement goals and activities.
* Develop and maintain strong rapport with employees and tenants to elicit feedback for continuous improvement ensuring organizational effectiveness.
* Assure organization\-wide compliance with all Federal, State and Local laws, ordinances, and codes relating to the operation and safety of facilities and staff; assures mandated inspections and repairs of fire safety/suppression systems and other such systems are completed, as required.
* Develop and maintain a house\-wide preventative maintenance program.
* Oversee Biomedical vendor and annual assessment of in\-house feasibility.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**
--------------------------------


* Oversees all Building Operations (5 FTEs), Environmental Services (15 FTEs), and Housing (3 FTEs).
	+ 510 east 62nd Street – Main Hospital – 75,000 square feet.
	+ 320 East 53rd Street – Resident\\Intern Housing – 60,000 square feet.
	+ 425 East 61st Street – Leased Office\\Administrative Space – 5,000 square feet.
	+ 425 East 61st Street – Leased Storage Space – 1,000 square feet.
	+ 1113 York Avenue – Leased Veterinary Care Space – 2,500 square feet

**Required Skills/Abilities**
-----------------------------


* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Excellent interpersonal and conflict resolution skills.
* Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
* Strong analytical and problem\-solving skills in qualitative and quantitative research.
* Proficient in Excel, Microsoft office, and other certifications as required by the Schwarzman Animal Medical Center.
* On\-call; after\-hours and emergency response availability when needed.

**Education and Experience**
----------------------------


* BA degree in Business Management, Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, or Facility Management from an accredited college or university.
* Ten (10\) years of management level work experience that has demonstrated effective leadership, technical knowledge, communication, and interpersonal skills, including understanding of and experience in budgeting, staff supervision, construction \& facility management, procurement, OSHA, ADA codes \& regulations, program development and project management at a multi\-building organization.
* Hospital and/or multi\-unit residential experience a plus.

**Physical Requirements:**
--------------------------


* Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
* The employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, crawl, and taste or smell.
* Employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.

**Benefits Package Includes**
-----------------------------


* Competitive salary
* Generous paid time off
* 50% discount on veterinary care
* Continuing education funds with rollover options
* 403(b) matching
* Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
* You may be eligible for The Public Loan Service Forgiveness Program as we are a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit employer

new_jobs.title: Executive Director - Mukti Mission US
new_jobs.description:
Executive Director \- Mukti Mission US
The Executive Director serves as the chief executive officer of Mukti Mission US is the public face of MMUS, and is responsible for advancing the organization's mission, strengthening donor and ministry partnerships, overseeing operations, and providing leadership for fundraising, communications, and organizational development. The Executive Director reports directly to the US Board of Directors and works collaboratively with donors, churches, volunteers, ministry partners, and Mukti Mission leadership in India.  

  

  



**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**  

**Leadership and Administration**

* Provide leadership for the day\-to\-day operations of Mukti Mission US.
* Recruit, train, supervise, coordinate, and support paid staff.
* Responsible for staff culture, performance management, and leadership development.
* Create annual goals, plans, and priorities consistent with the mission and direction established by the Board. Responsible for strategic planning and execution with measurable goals.
* Ensure effective administrative systems, policies, and procedures.

**Fundraising and Donor Development**

* Develop and implement strategies to increase financial support for Mukti Mission.
* Cultivate and maintain relationships with individual donors, churches, businesses, foundations, and ministry partners, with a focus on expanding the donor base and strengthening long\-term giving. Also, responsible for spearheading fundraising campaigns.
* Encourage engagement through prayer, giving, advocacy, and volunteer service.
* Manage CRM database \& integrate donation platform to website for funding campaigns.

**Partnership and International Relations**

* Serve as the primary liaison between Mukti Mission US and Mukti Mission in India, and facilitate communication and partnership while respecting the governance and leadership structures of Mukti Mission in India.
* Maintain current knowledge of ministry activities, projects, and priorities in India.
* Foster collaborative relationships with international councils and/or Executive Directors.

**Volunteer and Mission Team Coordination**

* Recruit, train, and coordinate volunteers and local ambassadors serving Mukti Mission US.
* Facilitate short\-term service opportunities and ministry\-related travel to India, when appropriate, in partnership with Mukti India.
* Represent Mukti Mission US at international Council meetings (once every 3 years), along with at least one annual site visit, and any other key events as requested by the Board.

**Communications, Events, and Ministry Promotion**

* Oversee the development and distribution of publications, prayer updates, newsletters, electronic communications, annual donor giving statements, sponsorship letters, and promotional materials. Promote awareness of Mukti's ministry, impact, and needs.
* Ensure effective use of digital platforms, including website and social media channels.
* Represent Mukti Mission US through speaking engagements and tables at relevant meetings, conferences, etc. Also responsible for hosting the annual Muk\-Tea event.

**Board Relations and Governance**

* Support the Board of Directors in fulfilling its governance responsibilities.
* Prepare materials and reports for Board meetings in consultation with the Executive Committee, and provide regular monthly updates regarding ministry activities, finances, and organizational performance to the board. Assist in the implementation of Board\-approved initiatives.
* Regularly engage with the Board Executive Committee on key issues facing the ministry.

**Financial Oversight and Compliance**

* Oversee accurate financial records, budget development, cash\-flow, internal controls, and risk management. Monitor ministry\-sponsored projects and donor\-designated funds.
* Ensure responsible stewardship of organizational resources.
* Maintain compliance with applicable legal, financial, and accountability standards, including IRS, State \& Federal 501(c)3 regulations and registrations, ECFA, and Candid requirements.
* Work with Board Treasurer and External Auditor on reporting and accountability.

  

**QUALIFICATIONS**

* Genuine commitment to evangelical Christianity, and the mission and vision of Mukti Mission U.S.
* 8\-10 years of experience in nonprofit ministry leadership, cross\-cultural ministry, nonprofit financial management, and fundraising.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, and excellent interpersonal skills.
* Demonstrated experience building relationships with donors, churches, volunteers, and community partners.
* Demonstrated technical proficiency with digital communication tools, CRM database management, website management, etc.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally, including periodic travel to India.
* Bachelor's degree in relevant field required; master’s degree preferred.

  

All candidates must be authorized to work in the U.S.; no visa sponsorships are offered.


This position is currently based in our New Jersey office, though we are open to a fully remote arrangement for the right candidate. Regardless of location, candidates should expect to travel domestically and internationally.


Applicants should submit their cover letter, resume, relevant work samples, and a list of 4 references (pastoral, supervisor, direct report, peer)

new_jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer - Heathcare
new_jobs.description:

* Develops short and long term strategies and tactics to assure operational and programmatic excellence, management and control.

* Responsible for Emergency Preparedness, Fire Drills and PCEPN
* Interpret clinic policies, objectives and operational procedures to department heads.

* Responsible for MIS system personnel and equipment placements
* Maintain professional affiliations and enhance professional development to keep pace with the trends in health care administration.
* Assist the Chief Executive Officer with planning, directing and coordinating facility activities to ensure full patient care based on clinic policies.

* Bachelors Degree required
* Masters, MBA, MPH or related post\-graduate degree preferred
* Three years experience in health administration including two years experience in a clinic environment.
* 10\+ years of senior management experience, with a minimum of 5 years leading one or more of the following functions: Customer Service, Claims, Enrollment, Operational Improvement, Value\-Based Contracting, or Sales \& Marketing
* 10\+ years of experience in a managed care/health care environment or a related government program
* Demonstrated experience successfully planning, organizing, managing and implementing Executive level projects


**Related Skills/Experience and requirements:**  

* Experience with government programs and their regulations, guidelines, and standards
* Exceptional executive leadership, strategic and day\-to\-day project and task management
* Demonstrated abilities in: Inductive Reasoning, Data Analytics, Employee Engagement, Conflict Resolution, Marketing Management and Provider Relationships
* Strong organizational and project management skills
* Excellent judgment and creative problem solving skills
* Solid understanding of physician practice operations including charge capture and clinical documentation;
* Outstanding listening and interpersonal skills with the ability to effectively work and communicate with providers and practice staff;
* Time management skills and attention to detail;


**Benefits Overview:** We offer attractive compensation with comprehensive benefits including: Medical, 401k Retirement Plan with discretionary Match, Free Life Insurance and Long\-Term Disability, Transportation Plan, Generous Paid Vacations and Holidays.

new_jobs.description:
Armory Center Program Director


The Police Athletic League (PAL) of New York City is an independent youth development nonprofit organization and has been a vibrant and vital institution, serving as an effective, critical bridge between police and communities across all five boroughs of the City since 1914\. PAL operates diverse programs for children as young as 2 years old to young adults. Programs include Head Start, after\-school programs and summer day camps for elementary, middle and high school youth, and summer Playstreets. PAL also runs evening teen centers and college readiness programs, youth employment, and juvenile justice programs. Staying true to PAL’s roots, a cornerstone of our youth development strategy includes offering competitive and recreational sports for children of all ages. At PAL, we’re devoted to empowering communities and building the best places to work, and that goes for our own teams too.


In its 110th year, PAL continues to reimagine the agency’s leadership structure to ensure the next 110 years are nimble, strategic, responsive, and efficient. We are looking for SONYC School Program Directors to elevate our out\-of\-school programming embedded within a New York City public school or PAL Center. Locations may serve Elementary through High School youth through SEL, STEM, Literacy, Sports, Arts, Mental Health, and College and Career Access Programming.


This position reports to the Borough Lead.


The Armory Center Program Director is a key on\-site supervisor managing all programming as well as relationships with youth, parents, school community, and the community at large. Directors must be creative programmers, skilled supervisors, and skilled talent developers. Familiarity with SACC regulations and DYCD funding requirements is a plus. Directors will partner with the NYPD, DOH, NYCHA, DYCD, NYCPS, and local community organizations. We are looking for individuals who can listen, problem solve and build bridges to partnerships that expand opportunities for NYC’s youth. As such:


* Candidates must be dedicated to learning and implementing Best Practices in the field of youth development.
* Candidates must be able to support programming that happens during the evenings, and weekends.
* Candidates must support the ideas and opportunities of the youth, staff, and community.
* Candidates must possess excellent communication and listening skills.
* Candidates must work together as a team to support PAL’s programming throughout the entire City.

Major Duties \& Responsibilities


* Foster social and emotional competencies and mental and physical well\-being in a safe, welcoming, inclusive, and nurturing environment.
* Manage all aspects of PAL Teen Afterschool Programming including overseeing the implementation of mental health support and inclusion coordination. Use identified resources to support youth with special needs and/or mental health needs, complete mental health referrals, and/or activate inclusion resources.
* Recruit, hire, and provide excellent supervision and support to all part\-time Group Leaders and Activity Specialists, Outreach Coordinators, and Content Specialists.
* Ensure the program is aligned to strategic objectives of PAL, policies and procedures, agency programming calendar, SACC regulations, and the contractual obligations of government and private funding sources including fire safety certification.
* Develops a strong Youth Development culture within the Center ensuring voice, growth, and advancement for all youth and staff. Train, conduct observations, and coach across all programs ensuring SEL, mental health, and inclusion policies are being implemented as designed.
* Coordinates with the Principal, Director, Regional Director, SYEP Director, and Head Quarters staff to grow creative programming opportunities unique to the Site.
* Collects program data, analyzes and drives PAL forward with data driven recommendations.
* Ensure strong reciprocal partnerships with NYPD, NYCPS school partner, DYCD, DOH and other Community partners aligned with PAL’s mission.
* Plans and coordinates various citywide programs, activities, and special events.
* Assists in the development of future funding grants and requests for proposals.
* Provides mediation and troubleshooting for on\-site issues.
* Respond appropriately when time\-sensitive mental health services are needed such as suicide prevention, grief, and loss due to death or incarceration of a family member.

What You Bring:


* An associate's in child development, education, physical education or recreation or related and two years of direct experience working with youth under 13 OR a NYS Children’s Program Administrator Credential and 2 years of experience working with youth under 13 OR a SACC Credential and 2 years of experience working with youth under 13 OR two years in college with 18 credits in child development, education, physical education or recreation or related and two years of direct experience working with youth under 13\.
* A minimum of 4 years of demonstrated successful experience in a supervisory position providing services to youth that includes program management and staff supervision with at least three years in a leadership capacity.
* Demonstrated skills in program planning, implementation, and evaluation.
* Open to learning and growing. All staff will be learning mental health, SEL, and special needs inclusion skills and expected to integrate them into programming.
* Knowledge of DYCD Connect preferred. Microsoft office skills are required.
* Strong verbal and written communication skills and ability to work collaboratively. Bi\-lingual in Spanish, French, or Chinese preferred.
* Able to travel to any PAL location in the 5 Boroughs for training.
* Work Schedule: Tuesday to Saturday, 1:00\-9:00pm with additional days as needed.

**Compensation:** The salary for this role is $68,000\-70,000 annually.

new_jobs.title: Executive Director – The Society of Wetland Scientists Professional Certification Program
new_jobs.description:
**Career Opportunity**

The Society of Wetland Scientists Professional Certification Program (SWSPCP) seeks a part\-time, contract Executive Director to administer their professional certification programs. The organization had previously been managed by an association management company but is now transitioning to direct management. An Armstrong McGuire interim manager has served in the role since February. The organization’s first Executive Director should be operationally and administratively skilled, comfortable guiding volunteer Boards, and have experience in budget and financial management.

**Mission:** SWSPCP’s mission is to certify wetland professionals who meet the highest standards for education, experience, and ethics in the practice of wetland science. The SWSPCP vision is to be THE globally recognized authority on certification of wetland professionals, requiring adherence to the highest standards in education, experience, and ethics in protecting and managing wetland resources and elevating the profession of wetland science.

**Reporting Structure**: The Executive Director reports to the Board of Directors.

**Total Staff and Budget**: The Executive Director is the primary staff person and may have flexibility to add administrative support/backup as needed. The annual budget is currently $250,000 \- $300,000 and the organization has more than $900,000 in reserves.

**Salary**: The monthly compensation is projected at $6,000, working 20\-30 hours per week.

**Working Environment/Location:** This is a remote position. SWSPCP is incorporated in North Carolina and maintains a virtual office in Durham. SWSPCP operates globally. The Executive Director can be situated anywhere in the United States, with the Southeast preferred. Occasional travel to meetings and industry events is required.

**Key Responsibilities of the Executive Director**Administration of Certification Programs

* Ensure new website and technology platform are successfully implemented.
* Engage with processing of applications/renewals as needed on new upgraded website.
* Properly filter and route questions from applicants/certificants to appropriate committees (Standards, Review, Renewal, Appeals, Ethics) for resolution.
* Recommend revisions to Standing Rules to provide clarity to applicants regarding requirements.
* Implement new Wetland Professional Certification Program intended primarily for international practitioners.

Board Management \& Governance

* Guide the board in process\-driven decision\-making.
* Ensure proposals for new initiatives align with mission and vision.
* Recommend and implement Standard Operating Procedures for critical areas, including investment management, sponsorships, and committee activities.
* Recommend updates to Bylaws and Standing Rules to adhere to good governance practices.
* Drive development of the strategic plan and business plan.
* Support Board, Executive Committee, and Committee meetings as needed.

Financial \& Budget Management

* Work with the Treasurer and Executive Committee to develop and manage yearly budget,; coordinate audit, and facilitate 990 filing.
* Process accounts receivable and accounts payable.
* Maintain monthly/quarterly financials within QuickBooks.
* Ensure the investment account is managed within investment policy parameters.
* Oversee contracting with vendors (technology, accounting, legal, etc.) as needed.

Marketing, Communications \& External Relations

* Actively promote certification programs to targeted audiences globally using appropriate media.
* Communicate organizational updates to certificants and other constituencies.
* Interact with Society of Wetland Scientists and other groups in the United States and internationally to provide value to the wetland scientist community.
* Serve as the staff representative to meetings and conferences.

**The Ideal Candidate Profile**

The ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications:

* Administrative and operational expertise to manage complex certification programs.
* Collaborative and professional leadership style to channel enthusiastic volunteer Board and committees toward productive activities.
* Astute financial management to ensure sustainability and growth of programs; oversight of budget, audit and investments; and ability to maximize ROI on promotional activities and new initiatives.
* Expert relationship\-builder to effectively manage internal volunteers/committees and key external constituencies in US and globally.
* Strategic mindset to take advantage of emerging opportunities while focusing on core mission.
* Interest in wetlands, environment, and professional development to align with mission.
* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional and lived experience.

**About SWSPCP**

For more than 30 years, the Society of Wetland Scientists Professional Certification Program has served the public's need to identify qualified individuals to assess and manage wetland resources around the world.

This program is intended to meet the needs of professional ecologists, hydrologists, soil scientists, educators, agency professionals, consultants, and others who practice wetland science. Three certifications are currently offered: Professional Wetland Scientist (PWS); Wetland Professional in Training (WPIT); and Wetland Professional (WP).

**Want to know more?** Visit wetlandcert.org. (*Note: new website is in development*.)

**How To Apply**

Join the SWSPCP and play a critical role in shaping its future while driving impactful change in the community.

**To apply,** click on the link for this position at **https://jobs.armstrongmcguire.com/.** You will see instructions for uploading your compelling cover letter, resume, and salary requirements. Cover letters should be responsive to the mission of SWSPCP as well as the stated responsibilities and qualifications.

Please provide all requested information to be considered. In case of any technical problems, contact talent@armstrong

new_jobs.title: Executive Director
new_jobs.description:
**Lead. Inspire. Connect. Transform.**



Sheboygan County Interfaith Organization (SCIO) is seeking an experienced, compassionate, and visionary **Executive Director** to lead our organization into its next chapter of growth and impact.



For more than 37 years, SCIO has worked to transform lives, one family at a time through our three impactful programs: the farmers market, Family Pathways supervised visitation program, and Bridgeway \& Beyond transitional living program. Our Executive Director will serve as the organization’s chief executive and public face, providing strategic leadership while building strong relationships with staff, Board members, donors, funders, faith communities, businesses, civic leaders, and community partners.



This is a dynamic leadership role for someone who enjoys both big\-picture strategy and hands\-on engagement. The ideal candidate is a strong fundraiser and relationship\-builder who is equally comfortable writing a grant, meeting with a donor, supporting staff, speaking to a community group, collaborating with the Board, or representing SCIO at a local event.


**Key Responsibilities****Organizational Leadership \& Operations**


* Provide overall leadership, strategic direction, and daily operational oversight of the organization.
* Lead program oversight, development, evaluation, and continuous improvement.
* Recruit, supervise, develop, and retain a strong team across all programs.
* Supervise and support the leadership team while fostering a collaborative, accountable, and mission\-driven culture.
* Oversee organizational finances, budgeting, compliance, resource allocation, risk management, and long\-term sustainability.


**Fundraising \& Resource Development**


* Lead fundraising and resource development, including donor cultivation, major gifts, special events, and revenue growth.
* Research, write, and manage grants and cultivate relationships with foundations, corporations, and private funders.


**Community \& Board Relations**


* Build and maintain strong relationships with faith communities, donors, businesses, civic leaders, social service organizations, and community partners.
* Work closely with the Board of Directors on governance, board management, strategic planning, financial oversight, fundraising, and organizational development.
* Serve as a visible ambassador and spokesperson for SCIO at community, civic, faith\-based, and professional events.
* Speak publicly and communicate effectively to inspire others to support SCIO’s mission.


**Strategic Growth \& Organizational Impact**


* Identify opportunities for collaboration, program growth, and increased community impact.
* Lead with a trauma\-focused, strength\-based approach and a strong commitment to diversity, inclusion, and equity.


**Qualifications****Education \& Experience**


* Bachelor’s degree or higher in human services, nonprofit management, business, public administration, or a related field.
* Four or more years of management or leadership experience in a nonprofit or community\-based organization.
* Demonstrated experience in fundraising, grant writing, donor relations, and/or resource development.
* Strong understanding of nonprofit operations, budgeting, financial management, and organizational sustainability.
* Desire to work with individuals and families experiencing poverty, homelessness, mental health challenges, substance use, social disenfranchisement, or other barriers to stability.
* Familiarity with Sheboygan County’s social service systems and community landscape is strongly preferred.


**Leadership \& Professional Skills**


* Exceptional communication, organizational, planning, and relationship\-building skills.
* Strategic and results\-oriented thinker who can set ambitious goals, measure performance, manage people and resources, meet deadlines, and make difficult decisions when necessary.
* Excellent public speaking and presentation skills with the ability to inspire, educate, and move people to action.
* Strong networking skills and enthusiasm for being visible and engaged in the community.
* Flexibility to occasionally work evenings and weekends for program needs, Board meetings, fundraising events, community engagements, and speaking opportunities


**Compensation \& Benefits**


* **Competitive salary: $70,000–$77,000 annually**, commensurate with experience and qualifications
* Paid holidays
* Paid sick leave
* Paid vacation leave

**NORTH \& CENTRAL ILLINOIS DIVISION**



JOB DESCRIPTION

At The Salvation Army, we are dedicated to “Doing the Most Good”. We are made up of thousands of officers, soldiers, staff, volunteers, donors, and partners working together to holistically meet the physical, emotional, and spiritual needs of our most vulnerable neighbors. The Deputy Director of Social Services serves as the second\-in\-command of the Social Services Department, working in close partnership with the Executive Director of Social Services to provide divisional leadership, continuity, and accountability across the department. * Coordinates with the Senior Directors of Program Operations, Mission Investment Management, and Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning to ensure regional counterparts are effectively connected to divisional resources, standards, and tools.
* Anticipates and responds to changes in the regional operating environment and ensures Regional Directors are positioned to adapt their teams accordingly.


**Impact Area Stewardship and Field Connectivity**

* Ensures Regional Directors serve as effective partners with site advisory boards, providing strategic guidance on program planning and community\-responsive program development within their impact areas.
* Ensures every active program site in each region has a clear and accessible regional point of contact for administrative support, program development, and capacity building.
* Monitors the effectiveness of Regional Directors and their teams across all three geographic regions for consistency, responsiveness, and quality of site support.
* Identifies patterns of field need across regions, ensures regional teams have what they need to support sites effectively, and escalates systemic issues to the Executive Director of Social Services.

* Supports Regional Directors in building and sustaining local stakeholder relationships that advance mission outcomes and increase community visibility for program sites.

As the chief executive of Be Noble Inc., the Executive Director will work alongside business leaders, elected officials, educational institutions, regional partners, investors, and community organizations to advance strategic initiatives that strengthen Noble County's economy and quality of life. Be Noble Inc. is Noble County's Local Economic Development Organization (LEDO), dedicated to fostering sustainable economic growth by supporting existing businesses, attracting new investment, strengthening the local workforce, and enhancing the quality of life throughout Noble County.

The Executive Director provides strategic leadership for the organization by:

* **Executive Leadership:** Provide strategic leadership by implementing the Board of Directors' vision, strategic plan, and annual work plan while serving as the primary liaison to the Board through governance support, committee coordination, board orientation, and organizational reporting. Direct the organization's daily operations, including staff, contractors, volunteers, financial management, budgeting, organizational performance, and policy implementation.

* **Fundraising:** Develop and execute fundraising strategies by cultivating investors, sponsors, donors, grants, and other financial resources to ensure the organization's long\-term sustainability.
* **Board \& Policy Governance:** Present policy recommendations to the Board of Directors and lead orientation for new board members and volunteers.
* **Brand \& Public Relations:** Lead marketing, branding, public relations, website content, social media, and public communications that promote Noble County as an exceptional place to live, work, invest, and do business. Represent Be Noble Inc. locally, regionally, and statewide as the organization's chief spokesperson and advocate for Noble County's economic development priorities.

**Who We're Looking For**

The ideal candidate is a relationship builder who thrives in a collaborative environment and has a passion for community and economic development. Successful candidates will demonstrate:

* Visionary leadership with the ability to execute strategic initiatives.
* Experience building partnerships across the public, private, nonprofit, and education sectors.
* Strong business acumen and organizational management skills.
* Proven success in fundraising, grant development, or investor relations.
* Excellent written, verbal, and public speaking skills.

* Bachelor's degree in economics, business administration, public administration, community development, or a related field preferred.

This is more than an executive leadership position. It is an opportunity to shape the future of Noble County by helping businesses grow, attracting new investment, developing the local workforce, strengthening communities, and improving the quality of life for current and future generations.

The Executive Director will work with an engaged Board of Directors and dedicated community partners who share a commitment to creating a thriving and prosperous Noble County.

new_jobs.description:
**Position Summary**

The Director of Philanthropy is a strategic and hands\-on fundraising leader responsible for advancing the High Line Canal Conservancy’s philanthropic goals and ensuring the long\-term financial sustainability of a dynamic nonprofit organization with an annual operating budget of approximately $2\.5 million. This frontline fundraising role manages a portfolio of major donors and prospects while leading all aspects of the organization's fundraising strategy including annual giving, major giving, planned giving, donor cultivation and stewardship. The Director of Philanthropy partners closely with the CEO, Board of Directors, and Leadership Team to promote a strong culture of philanthropy and achieve ambitious fundraising goals.

**High Line Canal Conservancy**

With over a decade of organizational growth and impact, the High Line Canal Conservancy is accelerating progress on the community’s vision for the High Line Canal’s 71 meandering miles by preserving and enhancing this cherished greenway that connects people to nature and binds communities together from the foothills to the plains.

This is an exciting time to join the Conservancy as it builds on the success of its recently completed $33 million capital campaign and enters a new phase of organizational growth and impact. Over the past decade, the Conservancy has established itself as a trusted partner, convener, and catalyst for advancing the vision of the High Line Canal through a unique public\-private partnership.

While the organization continues to mature, it remains driven by the creativity, ambition, and entrepreneurial spirit that have fueled its success from the beginning. As a regional advocate and member of the Leadership Team, the Director of Philanthropy will play a pivotal role in securing the required resources, relationships and community investment to continue to transform the Canal into a 71\-mile linear park.

**Primary Responsibilities**

**Fundraising Strategy and Organizational Leadership** 

· Develop and implement a comprehensive fundraising strategy that maximizes revenue, envisions strategic growth in all areas, and successfully advances organizational programs.

· Serve as a member of the organization's Leadership Team, contributing to organizational strategy, annual budgeting, cross\-departmental planning, and long\-term growth initiatives.

· Lead philanthropy program including major gifts, annual giving, corporate partnerships, foundation grants, planned giving, donor stewardship, and special events.

· Establish annual revenue goals, fundraising benchmarks, and key performance indicators across all fundraising programs in partnership with Leadership Team.

· Manage Philanthropy Department staff of two and ensure performance metrics are met.

· Oversee departmental systems, workflows, and fundraising operations to ensure efficiency and excellent donor service.

· Oversee grant prospecting, application, and reporting pipeline.

· Partner with the CEO on Board engagement, fundraising strategy, and organizational priorities.

· Ensure accurate revenue forecasting, pipeline management, and fundraising reporting.

· Meet annual fundraising goals through structured moves management process.

· Develop and implement a new legacy giving program to support long\-term sustainability.

**Major Gifts Fundraising** 

· Personally manage and grow a portfolio of approximately 75–125 major donor and prospect relationships, foundations, and institutional funders, developing tailored cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies for each.

· Conduct regular donor visits and qualification meetings.

· Guide and partner with the CEO and board of directors on major gift strategies and solicitations.

· Prepare compelling proposals, gift agreements, impact reports, and stewardship communication that align donor and foundation interests with organizational priorities.

**Special Events Fundraising** 

· Provide strategic leadership for the organization's two annual fundraising events, including a signature gala and community 5K race.

· Establish fundraising goals, sponsorship strategies, and donor engagement plans that maximize philanthropic revenue and community participation.

· Collaborate with staff, volunteers, sponsors, and volunteer committees to cultivate sponsorships, in\-kind donations, and leverage events to deepen donor relationships.

**Qualifications**

· Six years or more years of progressively responsible fundraising experience, including major gift fundraising.

· Demonstrated success personally soliciting and closing five\- and six\-figure gifts.

· Experience developing comprehensive organizational fundraising strategy.

· Experience managing donor portfolios using moves management principles.

· Experience supervising and developing fundraising staff.

· Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills.

· Experience using donor database/CRM systems and fundraising analytics. Raiser’s Edge experience preferred.

**Application Instructions** 

Qualified applicants are encouraged to apply by sending a resume with a cover letter addressing the applicant’s interest and qualifications for the position. Send both documents as one PDF attachment to employment@highlinecanal.org. No phone calls, please. The position will remain open until filled with a preferred application deadline of August 9 and preferred start date in mid\-September 2026\. All High Line Canal Conservancy employees are required to undergo a background check. This is an at\-will position.

Pay: $105,000\.00 \- $125,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Flexible schedule

* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Education:

Experience:

* Raiser's Edge: 1 year (Preferred)
* Major Gifts Fundraising: 6 years (Required)

***Join our vibrant community...***

  



Brethren Village is seeking an innovative and proactive executive to serve as our Chief Operating Officer (COO).

Brethren Village, a non\-profit Life Plan Community, is home to 1,200 Residents and employs 480 dedicated Team Members. Interested individuals are invited to visit www.bv.org to learn more about Brethren Village, and https://landinlancasterpa.com/ to learn more about the Lititz and Lancaster County areas.

  



Brethren Village's Chief Operating Officer will identify and advance strategic priorities; work collaboratively across the organization to drive innovation; help enhance service, efficiency, and effectiveness; help foster a positive and supportive workplace culture and a vibrant living community.

  



In conjunction with the President and other executives, the Chief Operating Officer will provide effective leadership and oversight for operations and staff; proactively identify opportunities, define priorities, and develop and implement short and long\-range plans aligned with the mission of the organization; help ensure sound fiscal management throughout the organization.

  


Primary responsibilities of the Chief Operating Officer include:  



* Participating in long and short\-range planning, and proactively identifying opportunities and challenges. In conjunction with the President, providing leadership for the development of the organization’s strategic plans; establishing priorities and specific objectives; ensuring plans are effectively implemented by managers.
* Fostering the highest standards of excellence with respect to the organization’s healthcare services, customer service / hospitality, safety and risk management, fiscal management, and other operations. In conjunction with the executive management team, overseeing and evaluating all services provided to Residents, on an ongoing basis.
* Establishing, tracking, and regularly reviewing relevant performance measures and benchmarks. Monitoring key financial and other performance indicators relevant to areas of responsibility; making decisions and taking action based on data / factual information.
* Proactively identifying opportunities to enhance service, increase efficiency, increase revenue, and control costs. Working collaboratively with managers to develop, implement, and complete specific process improvement projects.
* In conjunction with department managers, overseeing significant campus projects to help ensure such projects remain on\-budget and that quality, efficiency, and service objectives are achieved.
* Exploring and facilitating opportunities for collaboration / partnerships with external organizations and agencies to enhance services and/or manage costs.
* Working with the Vice President, Facilities, helping to determine optimal, future use of land and campus facilities.
* Working with the Director of IT, helping to ensure optimal use of technology and applications to enhance efficiency, control costs, and enhance service.
* Providing oversight and leadership for contracted Dining and Environmental Services, ensuring that service standards are maintained or exceeded, and budget targets are met. Overseeing service contracts.
* Providing effective leadership and management for assigned Team Members.
  



The Chief Operating Officer performs all work in an ethical manner aligned with Brethren Village's values, and consistently interacts with Residents, Team Members, and other members of the campus community in a professional manner. The Chief Operating Officer maintains open communication with Residents, Team Members, and other constituencies to foster trusting and productive relationships, and fosters positive relations within the broader community to enhance the reputation of the organization.

  


**Work Schedule:**

  


* Full\-time, benefits\-eligible: 40 hours per week, on\-site, plus additional hours as needed to fulfill responsibilities.
* Occasional evening and weekend work may be necessary.
* Occasional overnight travel may be required.
* The COO periodically serves “on\-call” and must remain available by phone or email to respond during emergency or urgent situations.

  


* A Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Business Administration, Healthcare Administration, Finance, Marketing, or a related field
* **Minimum 10 years’ progressively responsible** **management** **experience, including experience as an executive with a broad portfolio of responsibilities; proven ability to effectively lead and manage departments, programs, or functions and staff**

* A record of achievement \- the demonstrated ability to formulate short and long\-range strategic plans and achieve strategic objectives; effective experience managing or overseeing large projects; experience working through significant organizational challenges
* Thorough understanding of financial and economic concepts; ability to analyze financial statements and budget reports; experience budgeting for large departments or projects; ability to develop accurate financial projections and models
* A strong technology background or knowledge; ability to use technology to enhance efficiency

Position Summary

The Chief Development Officer (CDO) is a key executive leader responsible for building the Foundation's financial sustainability and long\-term growth. As a startup organization, the CDO's primary mission is to generate revenue that enables the Foundation to expand its programs, increase its impact, and achieve its strategic goals.

This role is responsible for creating and executing comprehensive fundraising and revenue\-generation strategies, developing strategic partnerships, securing grants, cultivating major donors, identifying new funding opportunities, and establishing systems that support sustainable growth. The CDO will work closely with the Founder, Executive Leadership Team, and Board of Directors to build a diversified funding portfolio and position the Foundation for long\-term success.

Key ResponsibilitiesRevenue Generation \& Growth

* Develop and execute a comprehensive revenue\-generation strategy aligned with the Foundation's mission and strategic objectives.
* Build multiple revenue streams, including individual giving, corporate sponsorships, grants, major gifts, planned giving, events, and earned\-income opportunities where appropriate.
* Establish annual fundraising goals, budgets, and performance metrics.
* Continuously identify innovative funding opportunities to increase financial sustainability.

Fundraising Strategy

* Design and lead annual fundraising campaigns.
* Develop donor acquisition, engagement, and retention strategies.
* Create donor stewardship programs that encourage long\-term giving.
* Monitor fundraising performance and adjust strategies to maximize results.

Major Gifts \& Donor Relations

* Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward major donors and philanthropic partners.
* Build relationships with high\-net\-worth individuals, family foundations, and community leaders.
* Prepare compelling proposals and presentations for prospective donors.
* Ensure exceptional donor experience and recognition.

Grants \& Institutional Funding

* Identify local, state, federal, and private grant opportunities.
* Lead grant strategy, proposal development, submission, and reporting.
* Ensure compliance with grant requirements and funding agreements.

Corporate Partnerships

* Develop strategic partnerships with corporations and businesses.
* Secure sponsorships for Foundation programs and events.
* Create mutually beneficial partnership opportunities that support both community impact and organizational growth.

Business Development \& Strategic Partnerships

* Identify opportunities that generate sustainable income for the Foundation.
* Develop collaborations with nonprofits, government agencies, educational institutions, and private organizations.
* Explore innovative revenue\-generating initiatives consistent with the Foundation's mission.

Marketing \& Brand Development

* Collaborate with Marketing and Communications to strengthen the Foundation's visibility.
* Support campaigns that increase donor engagement and public awareness.
* Represent the Foundation at networking events, conferences, and community functions.

Leadership \& Organizational Development

* Build and lead the Foundation's Development Department.
* Develop fundraising policies, procedures, and best practices.
* Recruit, mentor, and manage development staff as the organization grows.
* Present fundraising performance, forecasts, and strategic recommendations to executive leadership and the Board.

Financial Stewardship

* Develop annual development budgets and revenue forecasts.
* Track fundraising performance through key performance indicators (KPIs).
* Ensure transparency, accountability, and compliance with all fundraising regulations and ethical standards.

Startup Expectations

As an early\-stage Foundation, the Chief Development Officer is expected to be a hands\-on leader who can both develop strategy and execute it. This role requires creativity, entrepreneurial thinking, and a willingness to build systems, relationships, and fundraising programs from the ground up.

The CDO will play a critical role in transforming the Foundation from a startup organization into a financially sustainable nonprofit with diversified revenue sources and long\-term community impact.

QualificationsEducation

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, Communications, Marketing, or a related field.
* Master's degree preferred.

Experience

* 8–10\+ years of progressive experience in fundraising, development, business development, or nonprofit leadership.
* Proven track record of securing major gifts, grants, corporate sponsorships, and strategic partnerships.
* Experience building fundraising programs for growing or startup organizations is highly preferred.
* Experience working with executive leadership and Boards of Directors.

Preferred Skills

* Fundraising strategy
* Revenue generation
* Business development
* Grant writing and management
* Corporate partnership development
* Major gift solicitation
* Strategic planning
* Financial forecasting
* Public speaking and presentations
* Relationship management
* Leadership and team development
* CRM and donor management systems

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

* Annual fundraising revenue achieved
* Total unrestricted funds raised
* Major gifts secured
* Grant funding awarded
* Corporate sponsorship revenue
* Number of strategic partnerships established
* Donor acquisition and retention rates
* Revenue diversification
* Return on fundraising investment (ROI)
* Growth in the Foundation's annual operating budget
* Progress toward long\-term financial sustainability

Send CV/Resume to: cabangan@wendellman.org

Benefits:

* Flexible schedule

Work Location: Remote

**CHIEF OPERATING OFFICER**

**The Fried Center for the Advancement of Potential (FCAP)**

**Organization**

The Fried Center for the Advancement of Potential (FCAP)

**Position**

Chief Operating Officer

**Reports To**

Chairman, Board of Directors

**Classification**

Full\-Time, Exempt

**Location**

Crozet, VA — Hybrid; regular travel to partner university sites

**Salary Range**

$100,000 – $150,000, commensurate with experience

**ABOUT FCAP**

The Fried Center for the Advancement of Potential is a 501(c)(3\) nonprofit operating at the intersection of **healthcare education, disability inclusion, and preventive fitness.** Since 2016, FCAP has trained more than **100 undergraduate UVA student interns** — nearly all of whom have gone on to careers in healthcare — while delivering supervised, evidence\-based exercise interventions to clients with intellectual and developmental disabilities (IDD) and the general population.

Two clinics are currently operational, generating approximately **300 client visits per week.** FCAP is entering an ambitious expansion phase, with new university partner clinics planned at **Virginia Commonwealth University and William \& Mary**, and a long\-term goal of **15 university\-based programs nationally by 2035\.**

This is a rare opportunity to join a mission\-driven organization at an inflection point – one with a proven model, a unique and compelling story, a talented team, and the organizational will to grow.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Chief Operating Officer will build the business infrastructure to support FCAP’s expansion. This is a ground\-floor leadership role — part systems builder, part revenue strategist, and part chief of staff. The COO will design and oversee the business side of the organization: financial management, operations, university partnership agreements, communications, board operations, and operational scaffolding for each new clinic site.

The role is built to complement FCAP’s clinical leadership and to anchor its fundraising. Led by the Founding Clinical Director/President, the clinical team oversees the FCAP method, designs the curriculum, and ensures quality across sites. On the business side, the COO will implement FCAP’s revenue strategy, secure institutional commitments, and — in collaboration with the Chairman, Founding Clinical Director/President, and Board — cultivates and stewards major\-gift relationships.

The role requires close collaboration and consultation with the Founding Clinical Director to align FCAP’s clinical and operational functions, ensuring that business operations continually serve the nonprofit clinical mission. The COO will hire a Development Manager, who will run day\-to\-day fundraising execution, building the systems and pipeline for fundraising success.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Operations and Financial Infrastructure**

▪ Design and implement the administrative systems that let FCAP operate across multiple university sites: budgeting, payroll, HR, compliance, insurance, and data management.

▪ Establish financial controls, manage cash flow, track spending against budget, and produce regular financial reporting for the board.

▪ Build and maintain the operational playbook for launching each new clinic, coordinating logistics across clinical, university, and FCAP central stakeholders.

▪ Select and implement FCAP’s donor management platform and core development systems, which the Development Manager will then run day to day.

**University Partnerships and Agreements**

▪ Negotiate, document, and maintain partnership agreements and MOUs with university partners, vendors, and service providers.

▪ Structure each site’s financial partnership on FCAP’s cost\-share model and hold partners to a minimum five\-year commitment.

▪ Serve as the operational point of contact for university administrators throughout each clinic’s launch and ongoing operation.

**Revenue Strategy and Sustainability**

▪ Set FCAP’s overall revenue strategy and diversification plan, in close collaboration with the Chairman, Founding Clinical Director, and board.

▪ Oversee earned and institutional revenue — university contributions, fee\-based programming, CKC System sales, and corporate partnerships — and steward long\-term, endowment\-building goals that give each clinic and FCAP central durable footing.

▪ Lead FCAP’s development function and collaborate with the Chairman, Founding Clinical Director, and Board to oversee major\-gift cultivation and solicitation.

▪ Hire and manage the Development Manager to run day\-to\-day fundraising execution.

▪ Lead FCAP’s grant strategy, collaborating with the clinical team and Development Manager to identify grant opportunities, write and secure grants, complete necessary grant reports, and build relationships with grantmakers as needed.

**Communications and External Relations**

▪ Oversee FCAP’s communications strategy, including website management, digital presence, social media, branding, and public relations.

▪ Build and manage a student intern team that produces FCAP’s social media — giving students hands\-on experience while extending the organization’s reach.

▪ Work with the Founding Clinical Director and clinical team to translate program impact into clear narratives for funders, partners, and the public.

▪ Support FCAP’s professional certification and credentialing initiative as the model establishes a recognized professional pathway.

▪ Represent FCAP operationally with university administrators, community organizations, and external stakeholders.

**Board Operations and Governance**

▪ Collaborate with the Chairman to bring the current working board to the level of a strategic board.

▪ Manage board operations: prepare meeting materials, coordinate committee work, track action items, and support board recruitment and onboarding.

▪ Ensure compliance with nonprofit governance standards, IRS requirements, and state regulations.

**Title:** Chief Advancement Officer  

**Reports to:** Chief Executive Officer  

**Management:** Yes  

**Exempt:** Yes  

Annual Salary: $135,000 \- $150,000**About Boston Center for the Arts**
====================================


Boston Center for the Arts (BCA) is a multidisciplinary cultural campus in Boston’s South End, home to artist studios, arts organizations, exhibition and performance spaces that together create a dynamic ecosystem of creativity and programming.  

Through its residencies and initiatives, BCA serves as an epicenter for an expanding cohort of artists working across disciplines and has helped catalyze creative careers by providing fertile ground for experimentation, collaboration, and artistic risk\-taking. At the heart of the campus is the historic Cyclorama, whose distinctive 360\-degree form reflects a legacy of immersive storytelling and continues to inspire new experimentation at the intersection of art, technology, and public experience.  

At a time of significant institutional transformation, BCA is deepening partnerships with the City of Boston and cultural leaders across the region while advancing bold commitments in governance, artistic leadership, capital planning, and civic collaboration. Under the leadership of its CEO and first\-ever Artistic Director, BCA is building a more connected, artist\-centered, and partnership\-driven future for the organization and the broader creative community.**Position Concept**
--------------------


The Chief Advancement Officer (CAO) is a senior member of the leadership team responsible for driving philanthropic growth, strengthening the Boston Center for the Arts’ institutional brand, and expanding the organization’s visibility and engagement across Boston’s cultural and civic landscape.  

Reporting to the CEO, the CAO leads all advancement efforts, including major gifts, individual giving, foundation and corporate partnerships, marketing, communications, and institutional storytelling. This role plays a central part in shaping how BCA engages donors, audiences, artists, campus partners, and community stakeholders while advancing BCA’s role as a civic and cultural convener that amplifies the collective impact of artists, campus partners, and creative organizations.  

The CAO will work closely with the CEO, Artistic Director, and Board of Directors to cultivate major donors, activate board engagement in fundraising, and develop strategies that advance BCA's evolving role as a civic and cultural convener within Boston's creative ecosystem. As the organization's lead fundraising executive, the CAO will maintain a portfolio of major donors and prospects, personally solicit and close five\- and six\-figure gifts, and drive a comprehensive advancement strategy that supports both annual operations and long\-term institutional growth.  

**Key Responsibilities**### **Major Gifts and Philanthropy**

* Build and manage a leadership giving pipeline valued at $1M\+ annually, with accountability for achieving defined contributed revenue targets and moving prospects through all stages of the donor lifecycle.
* Manage, develop, and expand a portfolio of leadership donors and prospects capable of making transformational gifts.
* Lead and drive the cultivation, stewardship, and solicitation of leadership gifts in partnership with the CEO and Artistic Director.
* Develop personalized engagement and stewardship strategies for high\-capacity donors.
* Strengthen long\-term donor relationships through thoughtful communication, engagement opportunities, and institutional stewardship.
* Partner with the CEO to develop annual fundraising goals, revenue projections, and performance metrics, regularly reporting progress against contributed revenue benchmarks.

### **Advancement Strategy**

* Develop and lead BCA’s comprehensive advancement strategy, including major gifts, annual giving, donor engagement, campaigns, and fundraising initiatives.
* Establish ambitious but achievable revenue goals and strategies to expand philanthropic support.
* Build and maintain a strong pipeline of major gift prospects and institutional supporters.
* Partner with the CEO and senior leadership to align advancement priorities with organizational vision and strategic growth.

### **Board Engagement**

* Partner with the CEO to activate the Board of Directors in fundraising and donor engagement.
* Support board members in cultivating, stewarding, and soliciting donors and institutional supporters.
* Provide advancement updates, fundraising strategy, and campaign planning support to board committees and leadership.

### **Strategic Partnerships, Community Engagement, and External Relations**

* Build relationship\-based partnerships that amplify and connect the work taking place across BCA’s campus, including collaborations with campus partners, artists, and cultural organizations, strengthening BCA’s role as a collaborative civic and cultural platform within Boston’s creative ecosystem.
* Expand BCA’s presence within Boston’s philanthropic, civic, and cultural communities.
* Identify opportunities for cross\-sector partnerships, sponsorships, and collaborative initiatives aligned with BCA’s mission and strategic direction.
* Represent BCA at external events, convenings, and community engagements alongside the CEO and Artistic Director.


### **Marketing, Communications, and Institutional Brand**

* Oversee BCA’s marketing, communications, and institutional brand strategy across all public\-facing platforms.
* Guide institutional storytelling that amplifies the impact of BCA’s artists, programs, partnerships, and campus initiatives.
* Strengthen BCA’s visibility as a leading cultural hub and platform for civic and creative leadership.
* Ensure consistency of voice, messaging, and visual identity across organizational communications.
* Collaborate with leadership and program staff to translate artistic and civic initiatives into compelling public narrative

**Eastern Michigan University Foundation**  
In 1989, the Eastern Michigan University Regents founded the Eastern Michigan University Foundation, with the sole mission and purpose to provide additional financial support to students, programs, services, and the educational community of Eastern Michigan University. The EMU Foundation solicits funds on behalf of the University with the purpose of increasing the sources and amounts of private funds for the benefit of the University. All fundraising activities and events undertaken by individual units of EMU are coordinated through the EMU Foundation.

**Director of Development for The College of Arts and Sciences**  
The College of Arts and Sciences at Eastern Michigan University is the university's largest academic division, offering 124 degree programs with an average class size of 25\. It provides student\-centered education in the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, and fine arts across multiple campus buildings.

The Director of Development will provide direct support to the Dean and Faculty of the college while partnering with Advancement team members in a highly collaborative environment.

Reporting to the Associate Vice President for Advancement, with a focus on individual major giving, the Director of Development creates plans for donor outreach with the collaboration of Advancement team members. Additionally, leads, inspires, and manages annual resource development goals and multi\-year fundraising plan/strategy to support the college, students and faculty.

The Director of Development will be well supported by and will collaborate closely with the EMU Foundation's Advancement Services and Alumni Engagement teams. This includes direct fundraising support for annual giving programs, donor stewardship, and customized alumni engagement programming, event support, and communications to the constituencies from within the college. Additionally, they will work with the Data \& Information Systems team to utilize robust prospect research and development, reporting, and gift \& records support.

**Principal Duties and Responsibilities:**

*Fulfills Advancement Performance Standards*

* Invest 60\-80% of time on direct fundraising
* Manage a portfolio size, primary and secondary, of 100\-150 donors
* Have 160\-220 substantive interactions annually
* Perform 15\-25 qualification or discovery meetings
* Complete 15\-25 managed asks, with 10\-20 closed; and 7\-15 team asks
* Create an Annual Work Plan detailing: Division Priorities Goals, Job Specific Work Goals, Professional Development

*Donor Identification \& Research*

* Identify and qualify potential major gift donors.
* Conduct research on donor capacity, philanthropic interests, and giving history.
* Develop donor strategies based on wealth screenings and engagement analytics.

*Donor Cultivation \& Relationship Building*

* Build and maintain strong relationships with prospective and current major donors.
* Conduct one\-on\-one meetings, campus visits, and personalized engagement activities.
* Engage regional donors in alignment with institutional fundraising strategies.
* Work closely with the Dean, faculty, and institutional leadership to align donor interests with institutional priorities.

*Gift Solicitation \& Proposal Development*

* Develop tailored solicitation strategies for individual donors.
* Present funding opportunities through personalized proposals and case statements.
* Make direct asks for major gifts through in\-person meetings, calls, and written proposals.

*Donor Stewardship \& Recognition*

* Ensure proper acknowledgment and appreciation of major donors through thank\-you letters, impact reports, and events.
* Provide ongoing engagement to deepen donor relationships and encourage future giving.
* Coordinate donor recognition programs, including naming opportunities and special acknowledgments.

*Collaboration with Institutional Stakeholders*

* Work closely with university leadership, advancement team members, and faculty to align fundraising goals.
* Partner with alumni relations, planned giving, and corporate/foundation relations teams to maximize donor engagement.
* Serve as a liaison between donors and institutional programs or projects they support.

*Data Management \& Reporting*

* Maintain accurate donor records and track engagement activity using CRM tools (Raiser’s Edge).
* Prepare reports on progress toward fundraising goals and donor pipeline development.
* Use data analytics to refine donor strategies and measure success.

*Event Participation \& Major Gift Campaigns*

* Support or organize donor cultivation events, including receptions, galas, and campus tours.
* Participate in campaign planning for capital projects, scholarships, endowments, and special initiatives.
* Coordinate follow\-up strategies post\-events to convert engaged donors into major contributors.

* Communication: Strong verbal and written skills for donor meetings, proposals, and presentations.
* Strategic Thinking: Ability to align donor interests with institutional priorities.
* Persuasion \& Negotiation: Comfort with making direct gift solicitations and closing major donations.
* Confidentiality \& Ethics: Knowledge of fundraising best practices, gift agreements, and donor confidentiality.

This is a full\-time, office\-based position in the Washington, DC area, with approximately 50% travel and additional travel as required for the role.  



  

Reports to: the Board of Relief International USA, working closely with the Relief International Network Leadership Team.  



  

Salary range: US$170,000 to US$180,000 per annum plus performance bonus and benefits.  



  

Contract: Permanent, full\-time.  



  

This role is classified as requiring enhanced pre\-employment checks.  



  

**About Relief International**

Relief International (RI) is an international non\-profit organization that partners with communities impacted by conflict, climate change and disaster to save lives, build greater resilience and promote long\-term health and wellbeing. We work in 16 countries across Africa, Asia, and the Middle East, providing Health and Nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene), Education and Livelihoods programming that creates the foundation for community resilience.  



**About the Opportunity**

This senior leadership role manages the Relief International US entity. Reporting to the Board of Relief International USA, you will build and deliver the strategy that grows and diversifies our US donor base and oversee US grants.


Your first priority is to build a strong and varied pipeline of US income across philanthropy, institutional donors and the private sector, and to turn it into reliable, flexible funding. You will also oversee all US grants, hold legal and fiduciary responsibility for the US entity, and represent Relief International to US policymakers and partners.


As an experienced fundraising leader with a creative, entrepreneurial approach, you will open new doors with major donors, foundations, corporate partners and institutional funders, while also leading advocacy and policy engagement with US government stakeholders.
