new_jobs.description:
**About Us**

Maine Woodland Owners began in 1975 as a grassroots effort to share forestry expertise across landowners. Over fifty years, we have evolved into a highly respected, statewide organization dedicated to the conservation and sustainable management of Maine's working woods. We are widely recognized for our unique ability to connect directly with small, private landowners; our exceptionally high standards for forest management; and our top\-notch educational resources, including hands\-on workshops, community events, and an in\-depth monthly publication for our members. Through education, advocacy, and a growing land trust program, the organization serves thousands of members and plays a unique role in the state’s conservation landscape.

**Position Summary**

Maine Woodland Owners is seeking its first Director of Development to build and lead a comprehensive fundraising program that supports and expands the organization’s mission. This is a unique opportunity to shape the development function at a pivotal moment, leveraging a strong membership base, a compelling conservation mission, and growing land protection efforts.

The Director of Development will design and implement strategies across annual giving, major gifts, membership integration, and foundation support. The role requires both strategic leadership and hands\-on execution. We are a small and collaborative team; this position will work closely with the Executive Director, Director of Communications \& Outreach, and Office Manager, as well as program staff and the Board of Directors.

We recognize that the year\-end giving season is around the corner. Our leadership team is already laying the groundwork for our annual appeal so our incoming Director is walking into a supported transition rather than a high\-stress sprint.

**Key Responsibilities**

Fundraising Strategy \& Leadership

* Develop and execute a multi\-year fundraising strategy aligned with organizational goals.
* Establish clear revenue targets across membership, annual fund, major gifts, and grants.
* Partner with the Executive Director and Board to position philanthropy as a core organizational priority.

Annual Fund \& Membership Integration

* Integrate membership and fundraising strategies to deepen engagement and increase giving.
* Strengthen and grow the annual giving program, including appeals and donor stewardship.
* Expand and manage a recurring/monthly giving program.

Major Gifts \& Land Conservation Program Development

* Build a portfolio of individual donors capable of making significant gifts.
* Identify, cultivate, and solicit major donors and prospects.
* Help establish planned giving and land\-based gift strategies over time.
* Support and guide the Executive Director and Board in donor engagement and solicitations.

Grants \& Institutional Funding

* Identify and pursue foundation, corporate, and public funding opportunities.
* Build business sponsorships and corporate partnerships aligned with our mission.
* Manage grant writing, corporate outreach, reporting, and funder relationships.

Systems \& Operations

* Assess and strengthen Bloomerang member and donor database system and data integrity.
* Implement donor segmentation and tracking for effective relationship management.
* Establish metrics and reporting to track fundraising performance.

**Longevity \& Success**

You will not be judged on perfection, but on momentum and structure\-building. How we will support this role:

* Shared operational support: Our Office Manager assists with gift processing, database entry, and mailings, freeing the Director to focus on strategic fundraising and donor relationships.
* Collaborative leadership: The Executive Director and Board actively participate in donor cultivation and solicitations. You won’t be fundraising in isolation.
* Phased priorities: We recognize one person cannot build every system at once. The first year will focus on creating a structured annual fundraising plan, database health and systems efficiency, annual giving, upgrading our existing member base, and engaging top donors, with newer initiatives phased in over time.

**Qualifications**

Required

* 5\+ years of nonprofit fundraising experience, including major gifts.
* Demonstrated success building or growing fundraising programs.
* Strong relationship\-building and communication skills.
* Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands\-on execution.
* Experience with Bloomerang CRM and/or other database tools.

new_jobs.title: 340B Program Director
new_jobs.description:
**Job Description Summary:**

**Job Description:**


The 340B Program Director is responsible for leadership of the pharmacy 340B drug discount program for all qualified entities, CHC pharmacies, external vendors, and between the contracted pharmacies. Such leadership and coordination includes ensuring compliance with all federal regulations and related interpretations, ensuring the program is fully implemented in all areas of qualified use, and ensuring records and documentation are complete and accurate. The Director is responsible for data analysis to enable CHCI, its patients and pharmacy customers to receive maximum benefit from the 340B program.

**340B Program Director General Duties**

* Serves as CHCI’s compliance expert on 340B Program details, policies and procedures.
* Acts as the liaison with necessary affiliated departments and CHC pharmacies to ensure 340B Program integrity.
* Leads CHCI’s 340B oversight committee, which includes members from leadership, pharmacy, compliance, legal and finance.
* Provides expertise with the 340B Program to staff and participants regarding ongoing compliance.
* Develops and maintains internal relationships: Medical (CMO/CNO/CPO, pharmacy management), Finance, Operations and Legal, as well as external relationships (wholesalers, manufacturers, contract pharmacies, and third\-party administrator (TPA) vendors) as needed.
* Actively engages with CHCI leadership and participates in decision\-making processes related to the implementation of new 340B processes.

**Policy and Procedure Development**

* Ensures that policies and procedures are developed, implemented and maintained according to organizational, regional, national, state, and federal requirements and guidelines and are approved by CHCI’s legal department.
* Establish consistent policies and procedures for 340B that ensure productivity and efficiency so that long\-term management of the program does not hamper operations or create unnecessary cost.

**Education**

* Provides ongoing training, education and communication in collaboration with pharmacy and medical team required for the 340B Program at CHCI.
* Develops training/competency materials for all employees who work with the 340B Program.
* May assist in the development, implementation, or promotion of programmatic resource/tools to support staff.
* Regularly communicates with all staff involved with the 340B Program to be sure that processes remain efficient to address any problems or suggestions for improvement.
* Establishes a clear way for CHCI staff to communicate concerns to the manager.

**Regulatory Surveillance and Compliance**

* Monitors and assesses 340B regulations, guidance and /or rule changes, including, but not limited to HRSA/OPA rules and Medicaid changes. Ensure ongoing compliance with all applicable requirements
* Attends regular 340B training and shares lessons and hot topics with staff.
* Routinely monitors industry publications and websites as well as the professional media, literature, and peers to ensure CHCI has latest information regarding interpretations, rulings, suggestions and advanced ideas for improving participation.
* Provides expertise on all 340B Program legislation and policy changes from HRSA and OPA, informing and collaborating with legal and compliance teams.
* Collaborates with the Prime Vendor Program, pharmacy leadership, and other 340B institutions to determine the most appropriate use of 340B Program staff.

**Registration/Recertification**

* Responsible for ensuring that the annual HRSA recertification is completed within the allowable time frame.
* Responsible for ensuring that the HRSA 340B OPAIS (Office of Pharmacy Affairs Information System) is accurate for all organization entities.
* Responsible for ensuring registration of any new associated sites are within the allowable time frame.

**Self\-Audits**

* Develops, executes, and documents self\-audits of the 340B process. Coordinates and ensures remediation of findings.
* Conducts and/or coordinates and annual audit of all CHC and contract pharmacies. Documents results and follow\-up on any findings.
* Reviews and monitors all points of service where 340B participation occurs to ensure policy and procedure compliance, covered entity eligibility, and “covered patient” eligibility.
* Responsible for managing and troubleshooting pharmacy billing issues and ensuring that adequate system checks are reviewed to prevent billing issues.
* Monitors utilization records and 340B purchasing accounts to ensure that software/tools are working properly and accurately, performing audits or compliance assessments internally as needed; coordinates external compliance assessments with outside firms, when appropriate, to validate internal processes.
* Monitors 340B compliance within workflow processes.
* Responsible for the day\-to\-day management, compliance review, and operations of clinic\-administered medications and prescriptions filled by 340B CHC and contract pharmacies.
* Conducts monthly audits of all 340B\-eligible locations to verify adherence with the 340B Program guidelines/policies.
* Ensures compliance with all aspects of the 340B Program and implements all applicable aspects of HRSA’s OPA guidance, as well as CHCI’s policies and procedures.
* Ensure that audits follow current regulatory compliance recommendations and are completed at the site level.
* Ensures evaluations are completed for gaps at the site level and assists in providing the tools necessary to be compliant with the 340B Program.
* Evaluates covered entity compliance at the CHC and contract pharmacy and wholesaler levels.
* Performs annual independent compliance audits and reports findings to responsible representatives at CHCI.
* Performs 340B purchasing and utilization audits or compliance assessments internally, as needed.
* Routinely audits all 340B Programs to ensure compliance with regulations related to 340B purchasing.

* Present investment recommendations, strategic priorities, and performance updates to senior leadership.

* Lead executive\-level communications, governance forums, business reviews, and strategic planning processes.
* Balance regulatory requirements, operational capabilities, financial objectives, and stakeholder needs in highly complex decision\-making environments.


Team Leadership, Talent Development \& Organizational Excellence

The Executive Director of the Office of Rights, Compliance and Accountability (ORCA) provides strategic, university\-wide leadership to advance a safe, respectful, accessible, and welcoming learning and working environment while ensuring compliance with federal and state laws, Board of Regents Policy, and University regulations. ====================


The Director of Operations position is full\-time, 40 hours per week (exempt, benefits eligible). The Director of Operations reports to the Chief Operations Officer and provides leadership and operational support to Directors across all New Life Centers locations. This role oversees organization\-wide operations, ensuring effective execution of strategic priorities, operational excellence, and a collaborative, inclusive culture that empowers team members and drives organizational success. Will require some local travel (reimbursable). Pay commensurate with experience. This position is in\-person.

#### **Job Responsibilities**

#### **Operations Leadership \& Management**

* Direct and oversee daily operations across all New Life Centers locations, ensuring alignment with organizational goals, policies, and strategic priorities.
* Provide leadership and oversight for operational departments, including Information Technology, Office Management, Transportation, Safety, Facilities, and Events.
* Establish operational priorities and lead the achievement of short\- and long\-term goals.
* Serve as a primary point of contact for operational matters, responding to urgent issues as needed.
* Travel regularly between sites to provide support, oversight, and operational leadership.
* Lead or delegate operational responsibilities during site transitions, expansions, or relocations.

#### **Strategic Planning \& Process Improvement**

* Analyze organizational operations to identify opportunities for increased efficiency, effectiveness, and scalability.
* Research, develop, and recommend process improvements, systems, and operational solutions for executive review and approval.
* Lead organization\-wide implementation and adoption of new operational processes and systems.
* Balance site\-level operational needs with broader organizational objectives when developing solutions.
* Foster collaboration across locations and departments to strengthen organizational alignment and reduce operational silos.

#### **Team Leadership \& Development**

* Lead, coach, and support a team of Directors and operational staff, promoting accountability, ownership, and professional growth.
